title: Repair agreement and a comma splice
instructions: Choose the revision that corrects both the verb agreement and the clause boundary while preserving the cause-and-result relationship.

parts.prompt: Original: “The row of young plants need shade in the afternoon, the gardening team moves a screen beside them.” Which revision is correct?

options.text: The row of young plants needs shade in the afternoon, so the gardening team moves a screen beside them.
The row of young plants need shade in the afternoon; the gardening team moves a screen beside them.
Because the row of young plants needs shade in the afternoon. The gardening team moves a screen beside them.
The row of young plants needs shade in the afternoon, the gardening team moves a screen beside them.

choice_rationales.A: The singular head subject row takes needs, and comma plus so correctly joins the cause to its result.
choice_rationales.B: The semicolon repairs the boundary, but the singular head subject row still does not agree with need.
choice_rationales.C: Needs agrees with row, but the full stop leaves the because clause as a fragment.
choice_rationales.D: Needs agrees with row, but a comma alone still joins two independent clauses.

parts.hint: Check the head subject of the first clause, then decide how the two independent clauses express cause and result.
parts.correct_explanation: The head subject row requires needs, and comma plus so forms a valid boundary that preserves the result relationship.
